Mont Ventoux observatory runs a 60-cm reflector (2017) and a 20-cm outreach refractor, averaging 195 useful nights yearly (168 in 2024). Monthly data (~400 GB) transfers nightly to Marseille in 40 minutes. A new main camera (March 2025) has 30% lower read noise but needs an unapplied firmware update requiring one offline night.

Incidents: a 2023 dome-motor seizure bent a counterweight rod (replaced; limit switch added); a February 2025 clock offset lost three weeks of photometry (GPS checks now standard).

Rules: no observing during outreach evenings; raw frames compressed, never deleted, after two years; acquisition-software changes need a test night.

A proposed Spanish simultaneous-observation collaboration awaits evaluation of its shared scheduling tool and network capacity.
